scope: Final visible Draft; exact source/article/action/deployed bytes; core #627/#630-#637; daily-logger #549/#572-#583 and stack declarations; BookcaseDiscovery #104; all-state same-source review searches; current review schema/discovery; and held-candidate custody. Read-only review; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness, merge, workflow dispatch, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: The fourth merged PR did not harden FleetRunner
findings.location: Lines 6 and 15-26 say four PRs hardened FleetRunner, but identify only core #630/#632/#633 as FleetRunner changes; the fourth is daily-logger #578.
findings.explanation: Core #630, #632 and #633 are the three FleetRunner merges. Daily-logger #578 publishes the prior day's article and is not FleetRunner hardening.
findings.correction: Report three FleetRunner hardening PRs plus one daily-logger article-publication PR, not four FleetRunner-hardening PRs.

findings.title: The merged practice path does not exercise takeover
findings.location: Lines 11, 34 and 60 say #630 exercises the full stop/takeover path and closes the isolated-takeover acceptance condition.
findings.explanation: Core #637 says the current scheduled practice is readiness-only and never exercises takeover; it proposes the separate synthetic-job/fence-2 path. Core #627 records that the existing M3 practice ended with both workers HELD and positive terminal evidence unresolved.
findings.correction: Say #630 made scheduled stop/cleanup practice inspectable; do not claim it exercises takeover or closes an isolated-takeover gate, and retain #627's HELD result.

findings.title: PR #632 did not eliminate partial installs
findings.location: Line 42 says SemVer validation prevents a manifest-backed interrupted partial install from passing as clean and eliminates that partial-write class.
findings.explanation: Core #632 changes the version grammar and length bound so releases use a safe single folder name. Its source, reviews and tests do not change manifest-write ordering, interrupted-copy recovery or partial-install atomicity.
findings.correction: Limit the decision to safe SemVer folder validation before filesystem effects; do not claim it fixes interrupted partial writes or manifest atomicity.

findings.title: The journal and service dependency graph is reversed
findings.location: Lines 54, 66 and 80 call #576/#583 independently mergeable, put #572-#575 downstream of #577, and make #577 wait for all six smaller merges.
findings.explanation: The declared stack is #572→#573→#574→#575→#576→#580→#581→#582→#583. PR #577 is the consolidated integration candidate and says the smaller PRs remain review history rather than prerequisites that must merge separately.
findings.correction: Preserve the actual stack through #583 and treat #577 as the consolidated integration path, not a downstream PR waiting for separate merges of every smaller branch.

findings.title: Daily-logger #583 does not block core #634
findings.location: Lines 54, 64 and 80 say #583 blocks core #634 and creates a cross-repo sequencing dependency.
findings.explanation: Core #634 is a documentation-only pointer update designed for either current legacy or proposed shared-module layouts. Daily-logger #583 calls it a separate documentation follow-up, not a blocked dependent change.
findings.correction: Describe #634 as a separate pointer update compatible with either layout; do not gate it on #583 without an explicit base or owner decision.

findings.title: The cpuSlot bug and fix are misstated
findings.location: Lines 62 and 78-79 say rmSync leaves residual active-slot state and propose replacing the call with rmSync({ force: true }).
findings.explanation: Core #631 says unlinkSync(config.cpuSlot) throws ENOENT when the file is already absent, replacing an otherwise clean stop. Its proposed correction is rmSync(config.cpuSlot, { force: true }); the article's replacement omits the required path.
findings.correction: Record the ENOENT-on-an-already-absent-file mechanism and retain the required config.cpuSlot argument; keep the inaccurate held action non-dispatchable.

findings.title: Core #627 retains technical and owner gates
findings.location: Lines 68, 78 and 79 say #627 has no technical dependency, is Draft only by prioritization, and should be promoted and merged.
findings.explanation: Core #627 records both workers HELD during M3 teardown, unresolved cause and positive terminal evidence, and retained #307 tickets and human holds; it grants no runtime or merge authority.
findings.correction: Preserve the unresolved M3 evidence and existing human/owner gates; do not recommend readiness or merge without the recorded decision and evidence packet.

findings.title: Fixture PostgreSQL and authenticated controls are qualified
findings.location: Line 66 says no PostgreSQL or authenticated controls have been qualified.
findings.explanation: PR #572 records matched PostgreSQL restoration, #573 runs API/worker CLIs against a synthetic strict-TLS receiver, #574 qualifies that path inside the final image, and #577 integrates PostgreSQL command delivery and authenticated private HTTP controls while retaining later real-provider/deployment gates.
findings.correction: Separate qualified fixture PostgreSQL, private-TLS and authenticated-control paths from still-unqualified target-host deployment, real Langfuse readback, provider-backed drafting and public cutover.
